title: Response models and OpenAPI

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.
PURPOSE AND REAL-WORLD USE
`response_model` defines which fields the API returns, validates the result, and adds it to OpenAPI. This helps prevent accidental data exposure and gives clients a stable contract.

To run these examples locally, install `pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx` plus any extra package named in the lesson. Save the server example as `app.py` and start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. `--reload` is for development only.

WHERE DOES THIS APPEAR IN REAL LIFE?
A user record stores `password_hash`, but the response model exposes only `id` and `name`.
If this part is omitted: Without a response model, extra internal fields can leak and docs may be vague; make the return contract explicit.

spans.text:
LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI` — Imports FastAPI so the program can create its application object; without it, `FastAPI` is undefined.
`from pydantic import BaseModel` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`class UserPublic(BaseModel):` — Defines a Pydantic data model; its field types form the request-body contract.
`id: int` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`name: str` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`@app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=UserPublic)` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def read_user(user_id: int):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`return {"id": user_id, "name": "Ada", "password_hash": "never-return-this"}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
PRACTICE: CHECK IT WITH AN HTTP CLIENT
This complete file calls the app locally with TestClient; it does not open a server port. Install `httpx` for TestClient.
COMPLETE RUNNABLE CLIENT TEST
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class UserPublic(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str

@app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=UserPublic)
async def read_user(user_id: int):
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Ada", "password_hash": "never-return-this"}

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with TestClient(app) as client:
    response = client.get("/users/1")
    print(response.status_code, response.json())

spans.text: EXPECTED CLIENT-TEST OUTPUT

LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI` — Imports FastAPI so the program can create its application object; without it, `FastAPI` is undefined.
`from pydantic import BaseModel` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`class UserPublic(BaseModel):` — Defines a Pydantic data model; its field types form the request-body contract.
`id: int` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`name: str` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`@app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=UserPublic)` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def read_user(user_id: int):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`return {"id": user_id, "name": "Ada", "password_hash": "never-return-this"}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
`from fastapi.testclient import TestClient` — Imports TestClient so an HTTP request can exercise the app without opening a server port.
`with TestClient(app) as client:` — Creates a test HTTP client for the app and closes it when the context ends.
`response = client.get("/users/1")` — Sends the stated GET request through the test client and stores the response.
`print(response.status_code, response.json())` — Reads and prints both the HTTP status code and parsed JSON response.
COMMON MISTAKES
Returning a database object directly and assuming every field is public; define a separate response model.

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: Inspect `/openapi.json`, then test that an `internal_note` field absent from the model is not exposed.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: OpenAPI is a machine-readable contract from which `/docs` is generated. Documentation does not provide authentication or authorization.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: Use response models to exclude sensitive fields; a field missing from docs is not proof that the server hides it.
QUICK RECALL
Question: Which action best prevents the common mistake from this lesson?
Answer: Inspect `/openapi.json`, then test that an `internal_note` field absent from the model is not exposed.
